$comment: Stage 9 download tree. File names are the entire interop: a Swift side writing %03d, or keying a page by the reader's cache key instead of its number, produces a tree the other platform cannot read and no test catches until a user re-downloads a book. Both sides derive paths from THIS file, and `cases` below is asserted against both.

root.name: downloads
root.position: A sibling of cache/, both derived from the directory holding the database file: <db dir>/cache and <db dir>/downloads. NOT a tier inside it.
root.$comment: This is the load-bearing decision of the whole stage. PageCache can only build a path through DiskCache, which is rooted at the cache directory, so it structurally cannot reach a download — no eviction pass, tier purge, prefix purge or reconcile needs to remember to skip anything. Stage 8's ledger guards stay as a fence for the case where somebody parks a download file inside pages/ anyway; they are not the mechanism.

paddingRule: width = max(zeroPadWidth, digits(number)), so page 100000 is 100000.png rather than a name that collides with 0000.png. Four digits covers any book a person would read; the growth rule is what keeps the mapping injective.
extensionFrom: The container the bytes actually are (reader::integrity::Format::extension after the walk), falling back to `img` when nothing can be sniffed. Declared Content-Type is only a fallback, because it is what the server claims and the file is what the decoder will get.
safeKey: Keys become file names by keeping only [A-Za-z0-9._-] and mapping everything else to '_'; Komga ids are alphanumeric, so sanitising is about the server id a user typed, not about the book id.
